top_comments.author: @GEF6560AI
top_comments.text:
Andrew asked strong questions here, especially on whether Big Tech can be trusted with AI.

The core problem is regulatory lag. You cannot roll out technology with potential existential consequences, then check later whether the safety system was actually built. That is not governance. That is testing the bridge after traffic is already on it.

The agentic AI framing also feels too basic. Scheduling dinners and organising inboxes may be useful, but it reduces a network-level technology into a digital PA.

The real strategic value is not turning people into better calendar managers. It is making people more productive, especially creators, researchers, small businesses and independent operators.

Agentic AI is also a masterful data move. The more it helps, the more it learns. The more it learns, the harder it becomes to leave.

That is the chessboard people should be watching. I say this in all my lyrics: Humans are reduced to data streams.
